title: Coefficient-sensitive category-bar prism homotopy
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $C_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ deleting $U_{n-j}$, composing at internal vertices and restricting the coefficient only for $j=n$. Let $\mathcal D$ be small, let $v,w:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be functors and $\eta:v\Rightarrow w$ a natural transformation, let $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$ and $G\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal D,R}$, and let $t:F\to w^{-1}G$ be a natural map, with $w^{-1}$ denoting precomposition. Write $K(w,t)$ for the generator map $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(wU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$ and $K(v,G(\eta)t)$ for $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(vU_\bullet,G(\eta_{U_0})t_{U_0}x)$. Define $p_r$, $0\le r\le n$, by
$$(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\mapsto(vU_n\to\cdots\to vU_{n-r}\xrightarrow{\eta_{U_{n-r}}}wU_{n-r}\to\cdots\to wU_0,t_{U_0}x),$$
and $H_n=\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^rp_r:K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}\to K_{\mathcal D,R}(G)^{-n-1}$, $H_{-1}=0$. The prism identities are $d_jp_r=p_{r-1}d_j$ for $j<r$, $d_jp_r=p_rd_{j-1}$ for $j>r+1$, $d_{r+1}p_r=d_{r+1}p_{r+1}$ for $0\le r<n$, $d_0p_0=K(w,t)$, and $d_{n+1}p_n=K(v,G(\eta)t)$. They include the coefficient face. The resulting chain-homotopy equation is $dH+Hd=K(w,t)-K(v,G(\eta)t)$, including degree zero, where $dH_0(U,x)=(wU,t_Ux)-(vU,G(\eta_U)t_Ux)$. Thus the two maps are equal in $D(R)$. The same formulas and identities hold for a ring map $R\to S$, $G$ valued in $S$-modules and semilinear $t$, after scalar restriction. The construction allows identity arrows, empty categories, and arbitrary small categories without a finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), natural-transformation extension of its chain formula. Explicit prism maps, all face identities, coefficient endpoint and signs from returned steps 13 and 14; agent expansion, not asserted verbatim in Stacks.

proof.text: Write $a_i:U_i\to U_{i-1}$ and $y=t_{U_0}(x)$. A linear map out of each displayed summand extends uniquely to the direct sum by applying it to the finitely many nonzero components. This constructs each $p_r$ and both endpoint maps, even when different source chains have the same image chain. Their displayed formulas are linear in $x$. The coefficient transformation $s_U=G(\eta_U)t_U$ is natural: for $a:V\to U$, naturality $w(a)\eta_V=\eta_Uv(a)$ and contravariance give $G(v(a))s_U=G(\eta_V)G(w(a))t_U=G(\eta_V)t_VF(a)=s_VF(a)$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: For $i<j$, deleting vertex $j$ and then vertex $i$ gives the same shortened chain as deleting vertex $i$ and then vertex $j-1$. If adjacent arrows are composed, this uses associativity; if the coefficient vertex is deleted, the coefficient equality is $F(a_{k}a_{k+1})=F(a_{k+1})F(a_k)$. Thus $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ wherever two faces exist. In the square of the alternating differential these terms have signs $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and cancel. In degree zero the differential is zero, since the next term is zero. This verifies that $K$ is a cochain complex. A functor preserves compositions, so $K(w,t)$ commutes with all non-coefficient faces. On the coefficient face the required equality is $G(w(a_1))t_{U_0}=t_{U_1}F(a_1)$, exactly naturality of $t$. The same argument with the natural transformation $s$ from step 1 proves that $K(v,s)$ is a cochain map.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: If $j<r$, deleting the $j$-th vertex from the left of the prism deletes $vU_{n-j}$ before the crossing arrow. First deleting $U_{n-j}$ from the original chain moves the crossing position from $r$ to $r-1$. Both chains have the same arrows, by functoriality of $v$, and both retain $y$ at $wU_0$. Hence $d_jp_r=p_{r-1}d_j$. These inequalities exclude the coefficient face.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: If $j>r+1$ and $j<n+1$, the deleted vertex is strictly after the crossing and is not the coefficient vertex. Deleting it before insertion corresponds to face $j-1$ of the original chain; functoriality of $w$ gives $d_jp_r=p_rd_{j-1}$ with coefficient $y$. If $j=n+1>r+1$, necessarily $r<n$. Now the two coefficients are respectively $G(w(a_1))t_{U_0}x$ and $t_{U_1}F(a_1)x$, equal by naturality of $t$. The remaining chain is the same, including the crossing at $U_{n-r}$. This proves the same identity also for the coefficient face.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: For $0\le r<n$, put $k=n-r\ge1$. In $d_{r+1}p_r$ the segment from $vU_k$ to $wU_{k-1}$ is $w(a_k)\eta_{U_k}$. In $d_{r+1}p_{r+1}$ it is $\eta_{U_{k-1}}v(a_k)$. These arrows agree by naturality of $\eta$; all other vertices and arrows agree. Neither deletion removes the final coefficient vertex, so the coefficient is $y$ on both sides. Therefore $d_{r+1}p_r=d_{r+1}p_{r+1}$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: In $p_0$, deleting its first vertex $vU_n$ leaves precisely the all-$w$ chain with coefficient $t_{U_0}x$, so $d_0p_0=K(w,t)$. In $p_n$, the last arrow is $vU_0\xrightarrow{\eta_{U_0}}wU_0$. The last face deletes $wU_0$ and applies its restriction map; it therefore leaves the all-$v$ chain with coefficient $G(\eta_{U_0})t_{U_0}x$. Thus $d_{n+1}p_n=K(v,s)$. In particular this endpoint is a coefficient restriction, not an unchanged element.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, expand $dH_n+H_{n-1}d$ as $\sum_{r=0}^n\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^{r+j}d_jp_r+\sum_{q=0}^{n-1}\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^{q+i}p_qd_i$. Terms with $j<r$ in the first sum pair with $(q,i)=(r-1,j)$ in the second, with opposite signs. Terms with $j>r+1$ pair with $(q,i)=(r,j-1)$, also with opposite signs. This exhausts the second sum: its pair $(q,i)$ uses the first pairing if $i\le q$ and the second if $i>q$. The remaining mixed terms pair $d_{r+1}p_r$ with $d_{r+1}p_{r+1}$ for $0\le r<n$, with signs $-1$ and $+1$. Steps 3--5 identify every paired term, including its coefficient. Only $d_0p_0$ with sign $+1$ and $d_{n+1}p_n$ with sign $(-1)^{2n+1}=-1$ remain. Step 6 gives $dH_n+H_{n-1}d=K(w,t)-K(v,s)$.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: For $n=0$, $H_0(U,x)=(vU\xrightarrow{\eta_U}wU,t_Ux)$. Its boundary is $(wU,t_Ux)-(vU,G(\eta_U)t_Ux)$, while $H_{-1}d=0$. Thus the same homotopy equation holds in degree zero. All components in positive cochain degree are zero. The displayed $H$ is therefore a degree-$-1$ cochain homotopy on the whole complexes.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: Use the equivalent homotopy-category localization explicitly included in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $D(R)$ is obtained from complexes modulo chain homotopy by inverting quasi-isomorphisms. The equation in steps 7--8 identifies the classes of $K(w,t)$ and $K(v,s)$ in that homotopy category. Applying its localization functor preserves their equality, proving the asserted equality in $D(R)$. No assertion about a derived-colimit comparison is used here.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, generator formula; agent expansion to a natural transformation and its coefficient-sensitive prism.

proof.text: For a ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, give each $G(V)$ its restricted $R$-action $r\cdot z=\varphi(r)z$. Semilinearity of $t$ is exactly $R$-linearity for this action, and every $G$-restriction remains $R$-linear. A direct sum of these restricted modules is the restricted $S$-module direct sum: both have the same finitely supported tuples and the same operations. Thus every formula in steps 1--8 is literally the same $R$-linear formula; step 9 applies in $D(R)$ again. Smallness supplies sets of chains for every direct sum. Each $H_n$ has only $n+1$ terms, so no finiteness condition on the category is needed. Identities require no cancellation of degeneracies and are allowed as arrows throughout. If $\mathcal E$ is empty the source is zero and all identities are identities of zero maps; if $\mathcal D$ is empty the existence of $v,w$ forces this case.
